articles.headline: Tank Dell's first catch back sets up Marvin Harrison Jr's first TD with Texans
keyFacts: Tank Dell made his first catch since 2024, gaining 43 yards for the Houston Texans against the New York Giants in the second quarter.
The 43-yard reception set up Marvin Harrison Jr. to catch his first touchdown with the Texans six plays later.
The Texans converted a subsequent 2-point conversion to tie the game at 14-14 before halftime.
body: Amid an already strong start to his season, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has more weapons to work with in Houston’s offense.

Marvin Harrison Jr. made his Texans debut in Week 6 after being traded from the Arizona Cardinals. And on Sunday, Tank Dell played in his first game for the Texans since 2024 after a series of serious leg injuries derailed his promising young career.
Both made an impact for Houston against the New York Giants.

With the Giants holding a 14-6 lead in the second quarter, Stroud looked to Dell over the middle to start a two-minute drill. Dell caught the pass near midfield and ran into Giants territory for a 43-yard gain to the 30-yard line.
It's a bird. It's a plane. IT'S TANK DELL 🗣️
📺: @nflonfox pic.twitter.com/xK3LxkHwXd
— Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) October 25, 2026
The big gain was Dell’s first catch of the game and his first since Dec. 21, 2024. It set up Harrison for his first big moment with his new team.
Six plays later, Stroud found Harrison in the back of the end zone on third-and-goal for his first touchdown since joining the Texans.
Marv's first touchdown as a Texan‼️
📺: @nflonfox pic.twitter.com/tAqvn1N9fz
— Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) October 25, 2026
The Texans converted on an ensuing 2-point conversion and tied the game at 14-14 heading into halftime.

Harrison was a first-round pick by the Cardinals in 2024 after an All-America career at Ohio State catching passes from Stroud. He was pegged as a can’t-miss prospect, but the Cardinals gave up on him in this third NFL season by dealing him to the Texans.

Houston’s hoping that a reunion with Stroud can unlock the potential that largely went untapped in Arizona. Stroud, meanwhile, is seeking more of the same from his upgraded receiving corpshas he looks to lead the Texans from an 0-4 start into playoff contention.

articles.headline: Hose signs new three-year Worcestershire contract
keyFacts: Worcestershire batter Adam Hose signed a new three-year contract to stay with the county until the end of the 2029 season.
Hose stated that the team should aim to return to Division One and compete for all three trophies next season.
Head coach Alan Richardson described Hose as a genuine asset and one of the squad's most dependable figures.
body: Adam Hose has struck two hundreds and 14 half-centuries for Worcestershire including a career-best 266 against Hampshire in 2025 [Getty Images] Worcestershire batter Adam Hose has signed a new three-year contract to stay with the county until the end of the 2029 season.

The 34-year-old, who joined the Pears from rivals Warwickshire before the 2023 season, has scored more than 2,400 runs in 46 first-class appearances, featuring 96 times in all formats and was made captain of the T20 side half-way through this year's competition.

Worcestershire finished fifth in Division Two in 2026, with Hose scoring 638 runs with one century and five scores in excess of 50, having spent six months recovering from a serious ankle injury suffered while playing in The Hundred in August 2025.
Hose signed a three-year deal towards the end of 2024 that was due to run out next summer.
"It was a pretty easy deal to sort," Hose told the Worcestershire website.
"There's absolutely no reason why we shouldn't be setting our stall out to be back in Division One this time next year.
"In the white ball, we missed out very narrowly on a quarter-final place this year. There's no reason why we shouldn't be competing for all three trophies."
Head coach Alan Richardson said Hose was a "genuine asset" to the squad, growing into one of its "most dependable and valued figures".
"He has had a really tough and frustrating couple of years battling through injuries, but his resilience to fightback is very telling and says a lot about his character," Richardson added.
Hose is the second Worcestershire player to agree a new deal this month after wicketkeeper-batter Gareth Roderick signed on until 2028.

articles.headline: Reddit’s Largest Open Source Community Dumbfounded By AI Ban: ‘I Guess Linux Is No Longer Allowed Here?’
keyFacts: Reddit community r/opensource banned all AI-assisted projects and users who do not speak English.
Moderators stated that current AI tools are incompatible with their open source community.
Community members criticized the new rules for being too restrictive and unrelated to open source principles.
body: r/opensource, Redditâs primary âsubreddit for everything open source related,â has banned all AI-assisted and AI-related projects. The users on the subreddit are not taking the ban well. However, not all of the comments appear to be from LLM lovers, as the moderatorsâ decision to also ban users who âdon’t speak Englishâ has upset most of the community that supports the AI-related restrictions.

As reported by The Verge, the subredditâs October 24 post, titled âYour tokens aren’t valuable: No more AI,â features four new main rules: all projects must now be at least “1 year old,” have “multiple contributors,” be posted by someone who must “speak English,” and cannot be “made by” or “intended for” AI.

Thereâs a lot to go over here, but the ban on AI is simple; as the subredditâs moderators explain, âAI, as it exists today, is incongruent to this Open Source community.â Unsurprisingly, this is the part thatâs upset the majority of the users in the thread.

âThis is orthogonal to open source,â reads the top comment. âIt’s OK to not like AI but it doesn’t change whether something is open source or not. I guess Linux is no longer allowed here? Linus uses AI for kernel development now. This is a ridiculous stance.â

However, the moderator who posted the new guidelines stated in a separate comment that the overwhelmingly negative response is due to âsome guy on twitter claiming to be alternative newsâ who posted an âopinionated editorial pointing hundreds of people to the thread.â

Given the timing of when the thread was posted, alongside the fact that the X post in question mentions âthe Linux kernel,â they are presumably referring to this post by The Lunduke Journal. The moderator may be correct, as almost all of the top comments on the post are from users who have never posted in r/opensource before. The fact that Epic Gamesâ Tim Sweeney commented on The Lunduke Journalâs post also probably didnât help.

Yet, regardless of whether youâre pro-AI, anti-AI, or otherwise just ambivalent to AI, some of the users in the thread do raise some understandable concerns with the new rules. For instance, one user noted that their project, which has been âactively maintained for nine years, has 300+ stars on github, resolved dozens of issues for, and uses exactly zero AI,â would not be allowed on the subreddit anymore due to them being its âonly contributor.â

Likewise, many arenât too fond of r/opensourceâs new rule prohibiting all non-English speakers from the subreddit. âI’m a native English-speaker, but the no translated English point confounds me,â replied one user. âReddit is primarily USAmerican, yes, but there are people all over the world who use it. Google Translate is free. Why are we gate-keeping someone based on their English level and whether they used a translator to help them out?â

articles.headline: Ex-NFL punter turned California Democrat sparks fury with ‘racist’ banana stunt: ‘Toxic mockery’
keyFacts: California Democrats paid for a mailer depicting Latina Republican Assembly candidate Gracey Van Der Mark on a banana sticker.
The Orange County GOP condemned the mailer as racist, while Democratic candidate Chris Kluwe defended it as a criticism of her record.
Van Der Mark and Kluwe are competing for California's 72nd Assembly District seat in the November 3 general election.
body: California Democrats are facing backlash over a political mailer depicting a Latina Republican candidate as a banana sticker, with the Orange County GOP blasting the image as a racially degrading attack.
The mailer, paid for by the California Democratic Party, targets Gracey Van Der Mark, a Huntington Beach City Council member and Republican candidate for California’s 72nd Assembly District.

The front features a cluster of bananas with Van Der Mark’s face placed on a sticker resembling the Chiquita banana logo, alongside the message: “There’s a word for Gracey Van Der Mark’s Extreme Agenda…”

The reverse side doubles down on the fruit-themed jab, declaring her record is “absolutely bananas.”

The Republican Party of Orange County condemned the mailer as a racist attack, arguing the imagery takes on a more sinister meaning because Van Der Mark is the daughter of an Ecuadorian immigrant and also has Mexican heritage.
“The Republican Party of Orange County condemns in the strongest possible terms the racially degrading mailer recently deployed by the California Democratic Party,” the party said in a statement.

“By maliciously substituting the face of a female candidate with Latin American heritage (Ecuadoran and Mexican), Gracey Van Der Mark, onto the Chiquita banana logo, the Democrats have resorted to racist tropes.”
“This toxic brand of identity-based mockery has no place in this campaign,” the statement continued.

The OC GOP demanded Van Der Mark’s Democratic opponent, former NFL punter Chris Kluwe, speak out against the mailer and distance himself from what the party described as racial bigotry funded by his political allies.
Van Der Mark, who is seeking to defend the Republican-held seat against Kluwe in the Nov. 3 general election, said she would not allow the controversy to distract her from her campaign.

“As the daughter of an Ecuadorian immigrant, I take pride in my heritage and humble, working-class roots. I’ve faced attacks before, and I won’t be distracted by them. My focus remains where it belongs: fighting for California families, safer communities and a more affordable future,” Van Der Mark told the California Post.
But California Democratic Party Executive Director Melanie Ramil rejected the accusations of racism, arguing the mailer was intended to criticize Van Der Mark’s political record.

“The mailer is calling Gracey’s record bananas, but that was the nice way to say it. Her record is bigoted, corrupt and extreme. Gracey’s statements and ties to violent extremist groups have been condemned by civil rights groups,” Ramil said Friday.
She then turned the criticism back on Republicans, accusing them of ignoring immigration enforcement operations that Democrats have condemned.

“If the Republican Party of Orange County actually cared about the Latino American community, they would spend their time condemning the cruel and unconstitutional ICE operation terrorizing communities across the state instead,” Ramil said. “Voters won’t be deceived by this desperate attempt by Republicans when there is real work to be done.”
Kluwe, a former Seattle Seahawks punter who has since become an author and small-business owner, has defended the mailer as a criticism of Van Der Mark’s record rather than her heritage.
He has also accused Republicans of manufacturing outrage over the image because they fear losing a seat that has traditionally been considered safely Republican.
The 72nd Assembly District includes communities across Orange County, including Seal Beach, Huntington Beach, Newport Beach, Laguna Beach, Aliso Viejo, Laguna Woods and Lake Forest.
Van Der Mark and Kluwe are competing for the seat in the Nov. 3 election, with the dispute over the mailer adding another flashpoint to an already contentious campaign.

articles.headline: Barcelona v Real Madrid: El Clásico – live
keyFacts: Regional Catalan police reported 128 arrests for vandalism and looting overnight in Barcelona ahead of tonight's El Clásico match.
Real Madrid announced that goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois is ruled out due to the flu, with Andriy Lunin set to replace him.
Hansi Flick's Barcelona lead Real Madrid by six points in the league standings prior to tonight's 8pm GMT kickoff.
body: Tonight’s game also takes place against a weekend of unrest in Barcelona. There were 128 arrests overnight for acts of “vandalism, damage to public property and looting” in the city centre, according to the regional Catalan police.

The match is still going ahead, with an increased security presence already in place after the game was deemed “high-risk” by police last week. Back in 2019, this fixture was postponed due to protests in Barcelona.

We’ll have full team news shortly, but Real Madrid keeper Thibaut Courtois has already been ruled out of tonight’s game due to illness. “Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal (from the squad) due to a bout of the flu,” Madrid said in a statement. The Ukrainian goalkeeper Andriy Lunin is set to step in for Mourinho’s side.

Is the clásico making a comeback? A bitter rivalry that has raged for more than a century, Barcelona v Real Madrid may have been the world’s biggest sporting fixture during the era of Ronaldo and Messi, Mourinho and Guardiola. Incredibly skilful players dragged into extraordinarily spiteful on-pitch battles, each game felt like a heavyweight title fight.

These two teams remain the dominant forces in Spain, and their mutual hatred of one another is still very much intact. Still, the clásico has lost some of its intensity in recent years – but there are signs it may be coming back. Chief among those signs is Mourinho’s dramatic return to Real Madrid, where he is rebuilding the media war that wore both coaches out at the end of the rivalry’s unmissable age.

There is also, crucially, a touch of jeopardy about tonight’s game, particularly for the visitors. Hansi Flick’s Barcelona have started the league season with nine straight wins and are six points ahead of Madrid; that gap could be nine points, or three points, after tonight’s events at Camp Nou. The outcome may depend on Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé, two exceptional players poised to dominate this derby for the next decade.
In short, the biggest game in world football is back. Kick-off is at 8pm GMT, 9pm local time, so get comfortable.

articles.headline: Alaska Dem Mary Peltola in car crash during final sprint for Senate
keyFacts: Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola sustained minor injuries in a Saturday car crash, according to her campaign.
The accident forced Peltola to reschedule campaign events and temporarily delayed her eight-day Alaska Always Tour.
Peltola is currently running against incumbent Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan in a race that includes controversy over a candidate named Dan J. Sullivan.
body: Alaska Senate Democratic hopeful Mary Peltola suffered minor injuries in a car crash Saturday, temporarily sidelining her campaign, according to her team.

Peltola, 53, was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives Annual Banquet when her vehicle was hit by another car, forcing her to reschedule her campaign events slated for Sunday and Monday, her campaign said.
“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” said Cheryl Bruce, Peltola’s campaign manager, in a statement.

“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce said.
Peltola had been embarking on an eight-day “Alaska Always Tour” in the final days before the Nov. 3 election when the accident occurred.

The candidate, who served in Congress from early 2023 through early 2025, has a 1.2 percentage point edge over her rival, incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan (R-Alaska), according to the latest RealClearPolitics aggregate of polls.

The race has faced controversy thanks to retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan’s presence as a hopeful. Dubbed by critics as “Decoy Dan,” he has faced scrutiny for having a near-identical name to the incumbent senator.
Last week, the Justice Department sued to block the certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Sen. Sullivan loses because of “Decoy Dan.”
“Decoy Dan” is registered as a Republican, despite admitting he voted for Democrats in recent presidential election cycles, attended a “No Kings” rally and engaged in other left-leaning activity.

articles.headline: 187K+ fans call for EA to "Save Mass Effect"
keyFacts: A petition demanding continued development for the Mass Effect franchise has surpassed 187,000 signatures following BioWare's closure.
Petition organizer Joe Smith called on EA to properly fund the franchise or license the intellectual property to another studio.
The petition follows recent widespread job cuts by EA that also affected developers at Respawn, Maxis, and other studios.
body: A petition created to save BioWare's well-loved sci-fi RPG, Mass Effect, has topped 187,000 signatures.

We said a sad farewell to BioWare earlier this week. Job cuts, coming just months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn leveraged buyout of the company, were anticipated by experts, but drew widespread condemnation and messages of sympathy from across the industry.

Joe Smith, credited with starting the petition, isn't necessarily asking EA to change its mind about BioWare; instead, the petition calls for "decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect".
"This commitment requires proper funding, adequate staffing, and time allocation to maintain and advance the high standards the franchise is known for," the Change.Org page reads.
"Alternatively, EA could consider licensing the Mass Effect intellectual property (IP) to another studio that shares the passion and vision to keep it alive and allow it to flourish anew."

The petition adds: "Fans around the globe have invested thousands of hours exploring the galaxy, forming deep connections with its multifaceted characters and compelling storylines. It is a franchise that has transcended the typical gamer experience, creating a community that advocates for choice, individuality, and shared adventure. The potential cessation of new developments in this universe is a devastating prospect not only for fans but for the diversity of narrative-driven games as a whole."
Yesterday, we reported that a content creator claiming to have served on a BioWare community council shared alleged details about the cancelled next Mass Effect game, titled Mass Effect Universe.

In a lengthy Twitter/X post, the YouTuber claimed he'd had access through his role on the "Mass Effect Council", had seen firsthand what BioWare was developing, and had provided feedback during development.
This follows the appearance of an internal trailer for Mass Effect Universe, which BioWare later confirmed was real after the company’s closure and the game's cancellation.
EA's widespread job cuts also hit developers at Respawn, Maxis, Full Circle, EA Motive, and other EA-owned studios.

articles.headline: What does the bell icon mean on your CarPlay screen?
keyFacts: Engadget reported that the bell icon on Apple's CarPlay screen indicates that Siri is automatically announcing incoming messages.
Users can adjust announcement settings on their iPhone by navigating to Settings, Notifications, Announce Notifications, and then CarPlay.
Drivers can also manage alerts by setting up a Driving Focus mode on their iPhone under the Settings and Focus menu.
body: What does the bell icon mean on your CarPlay screen?
Demystifying one of CarPlay's least-obvious icons.

While some elements used in software design are so common that nearly everyone knows what they do (like share and search), others are more obtuse. You might have noticed this in Apple's CarPlay, which is intentionally simplified for the sake of reducing distractions. Yet there's a lot that goes unsaid: with the lack of a tutorial, you aren't shown how its multitasking works, never mind troubleshooting CarPlay problems or understanding what's new in the latest version.

One smaller CarPlay mystery is the nature of the bell icon that sometimes appears on the app switcher panel. It makes sense once it's explained, and it's easy to toggle its associated option. But Apple doesn't seem terribly invested in making this clear.
What CarPlay's bell icon actually means

As it turns out, Apple uses the bell icon to signal that Siri is automatically announcing incoming messages, whether from first- or third-party apps. This can be useful for keeping up with conversations without having to ask Siri yourself or check apps on your phone later once parked. At the same time, it can be annoying for noisy group chats, or when Siri repeatedly interrupts your music or podcasts. And when you're driving with passengers, they probably don't need to know what's going on in your Messages or WhatsApp conversations.

To adjust this feature, grab your iPhone and navigate to Settings > Notifications > Announce Notifications > CarPlay. When the general Announce Messages toggle is on, you'll find three additional options below. Remember Previous Setting is the default, but you can also force CarPlay to Announce or Silence incoming messages whenever it runs.

If you haven't already, you should also select which apps you want to allow announcements for under the Settings > Notifications > Announce Notifications menu. It's wise to limit announcements to apps without group chats, if possible. You'll want to know right away if your spouse will be late, but group chats are often full of trivial conversations that don't involve you. Disable announcements for other apps whose notifications don't matter while driving, like shopping and food apps.
You're driving a multi-ton death machine — the freer your mind is to focus on the road, the better.
You should be using Driving Focus anyway

In most cases, the better way of managing incoming alerts while on the road is setting up a Focus mode for driving. You can add and customize this mode on your iPhone by going to Settings > Focus. Tap Driving if it's there; if not, hit the Plus icon to add it.

Once it's active, you can customize this Focus to only allow calls and notifications from particular contacts while you're driving. You can also activate an auto-reply to let some people (or everyone) know you're busy. If you're worried about missing something, there's an Intelligent Breakthrough & Silencing toggle that may allow some other notifications to reach you if they're deemed important.

After configuring it, scroll down on the Driving Focus page and tap the While Driving button. There you can toggle Activate With CarPlay, which will switch the Focus on and off without you having to do anything manually. You can make the mode even more aggressive with the other options at the top, but those are designed for vehicles without CarPlay.

You may have to experiment to find what combination of Focus settings and message announcements works best for you. Though as we've suggested, it's smart to err on the side of receiving too few alerts rather than too many. It's rare that anything sent to your phone is more important than the task of driving.

articles.headline: Pressure grows on Sage as fans turn on Palace boss
keyFacts: Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage is facing mounting pressure after a 2-0 defeat to Newcastle left the team in the bottom four with seven points from eight games.
Sage stated that the internal atmosphere remains calm and he is focused on finding solutions, adding that fan boos are a normal reaction to poor results.
Pundits including Julien Laurens and Dion Dublin said Sage needs to be more ruthless and tougher to survive as a manager in the Premier League.
body: - Published

"Oliver Glasner achieved some amazing things, and now I have to do the same," Pierre Sage said after replacing the man who delivered an FA Cup, European trophy and Community Shield during two years in charge at Selhurst Park.
Four months into a three-year contract, the Frenchman is already under big pressure after a fifth defeat in eight Premier League games left the Eagles in the bottom four.

Palace have failed to win their past four games and Sunday's 2-0 home defeat by Newcastle was greeted with boos from home fans, who had turned up hoping to see a positive response after last weekend's 5-0 humiliation at fierce rivals Brighton.
"There is no noise inside the club," said Sage when asked about his future in his post-match media conference.
"The boos are normal because we don't have the result.
"The noise is the consequence of the result of the team, and at the moment we don't have what we expect.
"Inside, we are just really focused on solutions. How to be better, how to create the conditions to compete, and we will continue our work, and there's no noise inside."
Asked about boos from home fans during the match and at full-time, Sage accepted it was an expected response after failing to win.
"It's normal that people lose patience when you lose, because everybody wants to win. Today it was not the case."
Sage was named Ligue 1 manager of the year after leading Lens to a second-place finish as well as a French Cup triumph.
But could time already be running out for the 47-year-old?
Sage 'too nice at times'
Sage struck a defiant tone during his post-match media conference as he addressed questions about his future for 20 minutes.
"I don't have to convince the people around the club. I just have to convince the players to do their best to compete and to continue to improve," he added when asked further about his job.
"After that, this kind of decision is for the chairman, to the owners, this kind of person.
"For me, the noise around the team, the noise around the club, it's only noise."
Palace have just seven points from their first eight league games in the post-Glasner era.
After losing to Everton and Manchester City in their first two matches, Palace won at Fulham before losing at home to newly promoted Ipswich.
They secured a rare clean sheet in a goalless draw at Leeds before coming from behind to beat Nottingham Forest at Selhurst Park on 11 October.
That was their last win.
They have since lost at his former club Lyon in the Europa League, and Brighton, before drawing 2-2 against Besiktas in Istanbul on Thursday.
However, patience is clearly wearing thin after fans reacted to the latest defeat by Newcastle.
In addition, Palace have the worst defensive record in the Premier League after conceding 19 goals in eight games.
Their next Premier League match is at improving Tottenham next Saturday, before hosting Liverpool on 8 November going into the international break.
Palace's first game back is at fellow strugglers Coventry City on 21 November.
Will Sage still be in charge by then?
French football expert Julien Laurens said Sage needed to be more ruthless.
"He's a lovely guy. He's maybe a little bit too nice at times," Laurens, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, added.
"Remember when Crystal Palace beat Fulham earlier in the season? That was Palace's first win of the season and he felt sorry for Fulham.
"You don't feel sorry in this league. This Premier League is ruthless. It's the top, top level. This is the best league in the world.
"You can't feel sorry for the opposition you have just beaten, especially when this is your first win and you needed it badly.
"But this is the kind of guy that he is."
'No good being lovely with everything'
Sage's Lens side were built on aggressive pressing and a willingness to attack quickly once they won the ball back.
The Opta numbers showed a team intent on regaining possession high up the pitch.
Lens made 426 high turnovers during the 2025-26 season, frequently turning those moments into chances - producing 69 shots and seven goals.
However, Palace are clearly struggling to fire under Sage's leadership.
"He needs to do things slightly differently," added Laurens. "There is pressure everywhere in the Premier League."
Former Manchester United and England forward Dion Dublin said Sage needed to be tougher if he is to have a long-term future at Palace.
"It's no good being lovely with everything," added Dublin, also speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live.
"Things can't be lovely when you are a Premier League manager. You will just lose games and get sacked."
Former Leeds United forward Lucy Ward told 5 Live: "He has proved himself at Lyon and Lens. Being a little bit too nice doesn't help."

articles.headline: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey exits with injury vs. Falcons, is questionable to return
keyFacts: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey suffered a thigh injury against the Atlanta Falcons and is questionable to return.
McCaffrey recorded four carries for 29 yards with one touchdown and three receptions for 45 yards before leaving the game.
CBS Sports reported that the extent of the injury remains unknown while the 49ers lead the Falcons 14-12.
body: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey suffered a thigh injury and is questionable to return against the Atlanta Falcons. The four-time Pro Bowler went to the locker room shortly after going down, but he was able to jog under his own power as he went for further evaluation.
The extent of the injury is not yet known.

Before going down with the injury, CMC had four carries for 29 yards and one touchdown. He also had three receptions for 45 yards in the air. So far this season, he has 77 carries for 350 yards and seven touchdowns on the ground, along with 28 receptions for 190 yards in the air through six games.

McCaffrey is a dual-threat running back in quarterback Brock Purdy's offense and a reliable pass catcher. However, the 30-year-old has a history of injuries. The former Comeback Player of the Year had a PCL sprain, which sidelined him for five games in 2024; a pedal Achilles sprain that sidelined him for eight games the same year; a left calf strain that caused him to miss one game in 2023; and a pedal ankle sprain and thigh hamstring strain each sidelined him for five games in 2021.

The 49ers offense is already without wide receivers Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Demarcus Robinson (IR), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR) and Ricky Pearsall (IR). McCaffrey is a crucial part of this 49ers offense, and losing him for any amount of time is a big hit to their squad.

The running back room also includes rookie Kaelon Black and second-year RB Jordan James. Black currently leads the team in carries (11) and rushing yards (60) against Atlanta, and with McCaffrey out, he is expected to get more touches. McCaffrey leads the team in carries and rushing yards this season, with Black behind him and their QB third on the list.
With the exception of 2024, when he was limited to four games due to injury, McCaffrey has led the team in rushing yards, including two 1,000-plus yard seasons.

In his 10-year career, he has 1,735 rushes for 7,939 yards and 69 rushing touchdowns. McCaffrey was drafted in the first round of the 2017 NFL Draft, when the Carolina Panthers took him at No. 8 overall. He remained in the Queen City until 2022, when he joined the 49ers.
The Niners are currently up 14-12 against the Falcons as San Fran looks to stay undefeated.
CBS Sports will continue to update this article as more information becomes available.

articles.headline: When is the 2026 Ballon d’Or, who are the favourites, and how can you watch it?
keyFacts: The 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony will take place on Monday, October 26, at the London Palladium.
Harry Kane is the bookmakers’ favourite for the men’s award, while Alexia Putellas is the favourite for the women’s trophy.
Organisers said the ceremony moved outside France for the first time to honour 1956 inaugural winner Stanley Matthews.
body: The Ballon d’Or, football’s most prestigious individual honour, will be awarded on Monday, with Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe among the frontrunners in the men’s category and Spain’s Alexia Putellas the favourite to pick the women’s award for the third time.
Given to the best player of the 2025-26 season, the upcoming ceremony will mark the award’s 70th edition, and the first time it is held outside France.
Ahead of Monday’s official gala, here’s everything to know about the award, its history and more:
What is the Ballon d’Or?
The Ballon d’Or is the highest individual award given to a footballer, based on his or her performance in the previous season.
The award was created in 1956 by two sports writers, Gabriel Hanot and Jacques Ferran, from France Football, a French magazine.

Originally, the men’s award was limited to European players, but in 1995 it was expanded to include all players of any origin active at European clubs. Finally, in 2007, it became a global award with all professional footballers being eligible.
The women’s Ballon d’Or started in 2018 when Ada Hegerberg was named the inaugural winner.
The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) and Groupe Amaury – owners of France Football and L’Equipe – have co-organised the Ballon d’Or since the 2024 edition.
Who decides the Ballon d’Or winner?

The winner is chosen by an international jury of specialised journalists, with one representative per country: the top 100 nations according to the FIFA rankings for the men’s award, and the top 50 for the women’s award.
The FIFA ranking used is the one in effect at the time the nominee lists were published, which in this case was on September 8, 2026.
How does the voting work?
Each jury member selects 10 players in descending order of merit from a 30-player shortlist.

The list is then compiled by the editorial staff of France Football, members of L’Equipe’s editorial team, at least one member of the previous edition’s jury, and UEFA ambassadors Luis Figo and Fabio Capello for the men’s trophy, and Nadine Kessler for the women’s trophy.
The 10 selected players receive 15, 12, 10, 8, 7, 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 point respectively, based on the order of their rankings in the voting.
In the end, the Ballon d’Or is awarded to the player with the highest overall score.
What’s the voting criteria?
Players are judged for their performances over the whole of last season. For this year’s award, the timeline is from August 3, 2025, until July 19, 2026.
Jurors are asked to take three factors into consideration when ranking players. The Ballon d’Or regulations list the following in order of importance:
- Individual performances, decisive and impressive character
- Collective performances and titles won
- Class and fair play
Who is the favourite to win?

In the men’s category, England’s captain Kane, who scored an incredible 73 goals last season, is the bookmakers’ favourite to win the Ballon d’Or. As of Sunday, he holds about 70 percent of the market share.

Kane was the Bundesliga’s top scorer for the third year running and also earned a second European Golden Shoe. The 33-year-old won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich, and led England to a third-place finish at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Frenchman Mbappe, who won the Golden Boot at the World Cup and set an all-time goals record, is the second favourite, followed by teenage winger Lamine Yamal, who was part of Spain’s world title-winning squad.
The men’s 30-player star-studded shortlist also features Argentina’s 2022 World Cup winner Lionel Messi and the last two Ballon d’Or recipients, Ousmane Dembele and Rodri.
Who could win the Ballon d’Or Feminin?

For the women’s Ballon d’Or, Spain captain Alexia Putellas is the frontrunner after leading her previous club Barcelona to quadruple glory, which included the Liga F and Women’s Champions League crowns.
Putellas, who won the Ballon d’Or in 2021 and 2022, is hoping to match teammate and reigning winner Aitana Bonmati’s record of three trophies.

Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw, the Women’s Super League top scorer for a third campaign in a row, Barca’s Ewa Pajor, the women’s UCL top scorer, and Lyon’s Melchie Dumornay, who won a domestic treble, are also in the running.
Where and when is the Ballon d’Or ceremony?
The 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony will be held at the London Palladium on Monday, October 26, marking the first time it is being held in Britain.
Organisers said the decision to move the ceremony away from France, its usual host country, was made to pay tribute to the 1956 inaugural Ballon d’Or winner, England’s Stanley Matthews.
The red carpet will begin at 18:00 GMT and last for about an hour and a half.
It will be followed by the official ceremony at 20:00 GMT. France and Arsenal striker Thierry Henry and sports journalist Kate Scott will be the cohosts.
US rapper French Montana and English singer Jorja Smith will perform at the gala.
Where can I watch the ceremony and follow it online?
Al Jazeera Sport will have live coverage of the awards ceremony from 17:00 GMT.
DAZN will livestream the ceremony for free in most countries. Also, viewers in France can watch the ceremony on L’Equipe TV, while Telefonica will televise it in Spain.
Who has won the most Ballon d’Or awards?
Argentine legend Lionel Messi has a record eight Ballon d’Or awards in his trophy cabinet. He also holds the record for the most consecutive wins (four), taking the trophy home in 2009-2012.
His longtime rival, Cristiano Ronaldo, is second on the list, with five Ballon d’Ors.
France and Paris Saint-Germain forward Dembele won the 2025 Ballon d’Or, while Spain’s captain Rodri was the 2024 winner.
Which other awards are given at the Ballon d’Or?
A total of 13 awards will be presented on Monday, including the men’s and women’s Ballon d’Ors.
- Men’s and women’s Ballon d’Or
- Men’s and women’s Kopa Trophy (for U-21 players)
- Men’s and women’s Yashin Trophy (for best goalkeeper)
- Men’s and women’s Gerd Muller Trophy (for best striker)
- Men’s and women’s Johan Cruyff Trophy (for best coach)
- Men’s and women’s Club of the Year
- Socrates Award (for humanitarian work, charity projects, and social solidarity initiatives)

articles.headline: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile
keyFacts: Venezuelan opposition leader MarÃa Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after more than 10 months in exile, as confirmed by her ally Edmundo GonzÃ¡lez.
Machado's return followed the removal of former President NicolÃ¡s Maduro by US forces in January and subsequent political reconciliation talks supported by the US.
Machado's spokesperson stated that her return is a major step toward democratic transition and future free elections.
body: - Published
Venezuelan opposition leader MarÃa Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile.
"I am here. With you," Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail.
In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President NicolÃ¡s Maduro.
The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy RodrÃguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US.
Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands.

Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo GonzÃ¡lez, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: "I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear MarÃa Corina, is on Venezuelan soil."
"Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" GonzÃ¡lez said.
He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country "toward freedom".

An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted seven times to return to Venezuela, but was denied each time. There have been reports that the US was involved in delaying her return, which it has denied.

It's unclear what Machado plans to do next now that she's back, but she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held. Her ability to return to her country was always contingent on approval from the Trump administration, which it appears has now been granted.

A staunch supporter of democracy, Machado won an independent presidential primary election - held outside the Maduro government's official election authority - in 2023, earning more than 90% of the vote.

Despite winning the primary, Maduro's government barred Machado from running for office, accusing her of fraud and tax violations. Machado denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. She spent her final days in the country hiding in safehouses before her fleeing to Norway to accept the Nobel Prize.
In the 2024 election, Machado's ally GonzÃ¡lez ran in her place against Maduro.
The electoral authority, which is closely aligned with the government, declared Maduro the winner without making detailed voting tallies public.
The opposition argued that GonzÃ¡lez won the election, not Maduro, uploading copies of the voting tallies as evidence.
Maduro was removed from the country by US forces in January, and is currently jailed in New York where he faces drugs, weapons and torture charges. He has pleaded not guilty.
A spokesman for Machado called her return "a major step toward a democratic transition and free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections in the near future".

"We thank President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the US Government, Congress, and allied governments for their continued leadership and support," her spokesperson, David Smolansky, added.
Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump said, "I don't know anything about" her return, and added that he hoped she was "safe".
"I think she's a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize, so how can I say anything else? And I hope she's safe," he said.
In January, Machado visited the White House and gifted her Nobel prize award to Trump. The committee that issues the prize had said "it cannot be revoked, shared, or transferred to others".
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised his country's role in securing her return through political reconciliation talks.

"The conditions allowing for the safe return of Ms Machado to Venezuela is the direct result of the US supported reconciliation talks which has already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile," he posted on X.

He added: "We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy."

articles.headline: 'Save Mass Effect' petition hits over 180,000 signatures within days of BioWare's closure
keyFacts: Gaming giant EA shut down studio BioWare and canceled Mass Effect 5 following an acquisition by the Public Investment Fund and investment firms.
A change.org petition titled Save Mass Effect surpassed 180,000 verified signatures urging EA to continue the series or license the intellectual property.
Fans expressed devastation over the closure and shared memories of the franchise, though industry observers noted EA is unlikely to change its decision.
body: Last week, the other shoe dropped for legendary RPG studio BioWare: shortly after EA's acquisition by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, the gaming giant shut down BioWare and canceled Mass Effect 5.

Fans have spent the intervening days combing through the detritus of the next game in the series' leaked remains, and some have even signed a change.org petition to save the series. Right now, that #SaveMassEffect petition has hit over 180,000 verified signatures.

Notably it does not call for EA to walk back its decision to shut down BioWare. Instead, it's about keeping the Mass Effect series going: "We are urgently petitioning EA to take decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect," Joe Smith's plea reads. "Alternatively, EA could consider licensing the Mass Effect intellectual property to another studio that shares the passion and vision to keep it alive and allow it to flourish anew."

Of course, EA is not beholden to the demands of a digital petition—the chances that this will inspire a revolution of the heart throughout the industry's C-suites are not high. One could argue that, if the publisher held the legacy of Mass Effect or, indeed, the computer RPG itself as a priority, it would not have shut down BioWare in the first place. But this petition has proven a lightning rod of enthusiasm for fans of the series, who are sharing their memories of the games along with their signatures.

"You’re gonna have to pry Garrus from my cold dead hands," wrote Savannah. Another from Joe reads, "My wife and I absolutely love the Mass Effect series. We’ve had so many good times together sharing Commander Shepard's story over the years. It really devastated both of us when we heard that BioWare is done and, in turn, Mass Effect 5 wasn’t going to happen." Austin wrote: "The trilogy and even silly Andromeda has made a permanent impact on my life. I’ve been playing for 13 years."

While it's hard to imagine EA doing a 180 on this, it's also hard to imagine Mass Effect staying down for good (even if that might be where we're headed). Maybe Canada's New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis has the right idea, and BioWare should be publicly funded for the collective good. Either way, the immediate, broader future for games made under the EA banner looks a mite grim.

As time has passed, he's amassed a hefty backlog of retro shooters, CRPGs, and janky '90s esoterica. articles.headline: Furious Man United fan says he wants them to be RELEGATED in shock claim after latest humiliation
keyFacts: A Manchester United supporter told talkSPORT that he would not mind if the club was relegated to force ownership changes.

body: Manchester United can only return to their former glories if they are relegated from the Premier League.
That is according to one disgruntled supporter following Sunday’s chastening defeat at home to Bournemouth .
United are just a point above the relegation zone after losing to Bournemouth Getty
The Red Devils were beaten 3-0 at Old Trafford as their winless run in all competitions extended to eight matches.
Michael Carrick’s side now sit just a point above the relegation zone in 16th place.
A toxic atmosphere inside the stadium saw the players booed off at full-time as they were beaten by the Cherries.
Meanwhile, opposition to the Glazer family and INEOS’ ownership has now seen one United fan make a surprising admission over their top-flight status.
United fan wants club relegated
Following their latest defeat, Red Devils supporter Chris spoke to talkSPORT’s Sam Matterface on GameDay Live.
Expressing his frustration with the running of the club, Chris revealed: “I won’t be bothered if we get relegated.
“Literally, the only way the Glazers are going to go is if we stop making money.

“All these money men who are only involved in Man United because of the money, if you get rid of all of that, strip it back down to what actual proper United fans want, where we’re proud of the Busby Babes, Class of ‘92, Mancunians or young lads coming and playing for our team.
“All we get is has-beens coming to our team getting paid too much money. They’re not bothered. It’s like a place you come for two or three years, get paid and then just go wherever you want to go.
“The only way you get rid of all that is, and I won’t be bothered, if we went down. Scrap the new stadium, we’ll stay here.
United fan Chris fears relegation is needed to solve the club’s issues Getty
“The plastic fans who don’t want to be United fans, let them go and then we’ll start again, like (Matt) Busby did. That’s my view anyway.”

As for whether there is anything the fans can do to get their message across to the owners, he added: “I don’t know what the answer is because the problem is as well, do you know any other brand in the world where if all of us stop going now, all season ticket holders stop going, there would be other people who just go and queue up and go.
“It’s madness. It’s like we’re all intoxicated and we’re just going for it because we love the club and we want it back to what we wanted.
“There’s no perfect remedy, but I get what you’re saying. Something needs to happen. That’s why I’m saying something extreme where I won’t be bothered if we get relegated.
“I genuinely won’t be bothered because I’m sick of this. All the things I love about Man United or did, we’re starting to become a club I can’t stand.
“The morals of it, sacking decent people who have been at the club for years, all these little things now.
Carrick’s side have failed to win any of their last eight matches in all competitions Getty
“They make me cringe and that’s the club I go (to watch). My kids are now supporters.”
When were Man United last relegated?
United have not tasted relegation for 52 years having last dropped out of the top-flight in 1974.
On that occasion, the club secured an immediate return to the First Division and have remained at the same level since.
They came closest to dropping out of the Premier League as recently as two seasons ago, though.
The Red Devils finished 15th on 42 points in the 2024/25 campaign, their lowest top-flight points tally since the previous relegation.
Meanwhile, 102 of the 140 seasons in the club’s history have been spent at the highest level of English football.

articles.headline: Topping DX1 II review: a well-built DAC with great specification that just fails grab you by the lapels
keyFacts: The Topping DX1 II is a compact, aluminum-built DAC and headphone amplifier priced at $119 in the United States.
TechRadar reported that the device offers impressive detail, a robust specification, and a pleasant tonal balance, but noted a lack of dynamic punch and high-frequency roll-off.
The unit is available now and features dual ESS DACs, a remote control, and extensive options for user sound adjustment.
body: TechRadar Verdict

Its sound isn’t perfect, and it’s not without worthwhile competition, but when it comes to sonic detail and plenty of end-user options where performance is concerned, the Topping DX1 II has lots to recommend it. It looks and feels a cut above most of its price-comparable rivals, too.
Reasons to buy
- + Detailed, laid-back sound
- + Impressive specification
- + Very acceptable standard of build and finish
Reasons to avoid
- - Could easily sound more dynamic
- - Quite pronounced high-frequency roll-off
- - By no means your only choice
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Topping DX1 II: two-minute review

The world is not short of little DAC/headphone amps that want to bring a taste of authentic audio quality to your desktop experience — and here’s another one. The Topping DX1 II is a thorough update of a previous (and very competitive) in the Chinese brand's stable, and it makes a strong case for itself even before it’s started doing its thing.

The aluminum casework looks and feels good and the on-paper specification is difficult to lay a glove on. It includes — deep breath — a very hi-res ESS DAC, carefully considered digital and analog architecture, USB-C for both power and data, sufficient grunt to drive most headphones without difficulty, a fistful of input and output options (including balanced analog connectivity), and the facility for plenty of end-user input where sound is concerned. The standard of construction and finish is more than adequate. And a little remote control handset takes some of the pressure off an overworked physical control interface.

The difference the DX1 II can make to your audio experience when it sits between, say, your laptop and the headphones that are plugged into it is fairly profound. The Topping is by no means perfect — it doesn’t attack the top of the frequency range quite as willingly as it might, and it doesn’t have the heft to make big dynamic variations as apparent as they might be — but it’s a far more convincing and well-realized listen than your laptop alone has a hope of being. Soundstaging, rhythmic expression, detail levels and all-around musicality all enjoy a big uptick, and the way the DX1 II handles a tonal balance is one of the most uncomplicatedly enjoyable things about it.

The Topping DX1 II hasn’t closed the door on other desktop-friendly headphone amp/DAC units at similar money, but it’s certainly made sure it’s on the inside of the conversation for the best on the market.
Topping DX1 II review: Price & release date
- Announced on May 18, 2026 (with availability from late June/July 2026)
- Priced $119 / £119 (around AU$169)
The Topping DX1 II is on sale now, and in the United States it costs $119. It’s £119 in the United Kingdom, while in Australia it goes for around AU$169.
So, it's a little pricier than the oh-so-portable iFi Go Link Max and the bigger, hip-flask-esque iFi Uno, say, but an awful lot cheaper than the also-new iFi iDSD GR2.
What exactly are you getting for your money if you go for the Topping? Read on.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Topping DX1 II review: Features
- ESS ES9039Q2M DAC
- Balanced and unbalanced outputs
- UAC 1.0 and UAC 2.0
There’s something quite admirable about the way Topping has specified the DX1 II — I’ve used bigger and more expensive DAC/headphone amps that don’t come close to the level of this little device.

It’s built around a very capable ESS ES90392QM DAC chipset and features dual-DAC architecture with a dedicated digital-to-analog converter for each channel, plus fully independent processing. Digital files of up to 32bit/384kHz and DSD256 are supported.
A 16-core XMOS XU-316 assists with signal processing — just as with the dual-DAC arrangement and the fully balanced analog stage, the idea is to keep noise and distortion to an absolute minimum.

Digital audio information can be delivered using either the digital optical input or the USB-C slot on the rear of the Topping. The USB-C input also provides power to the device. Outputs consist of an unbalanced 3.5mm headphone socket, a couple of balanced 4.4mm alternatives (one for headphones, the other for connecting the DX1 II to a system, a powered speaker or what-have-you) and a line-level analog output on stereo RCAs.

There’s an optical output in case the digital signal needs to be preserved, and a switch to toggle between UAC 1.0 and UAC 2.0 — the first setting allows the Topping to be compatible with, say, the Nintendo Switch and the Sony PlayStation 5.

Topping has made provision for an awful lot of end-user input into the way the DX1 II performs. Connect it to a computer and you can access both the ‘Home Web’ platform (from where stuff like gain can be adjusted and no fewer than eight distinct digital filters are available) and ‘Topping Tune’. This uses a simple drag-n-drop interface to allow the user to easily create and adjust PEQ settings — frequency, gain and bandwidth control across 10 bands (with independent left and right channel adjustment) can be tweaked and settings saved. It’s available across each of the DX1 II’s outputs.
- Features score: 5 / 5
Topping DX1 II review: Sound quality
- Impressively detailed, easy-going sound
- Pleasant tonal balance
- Could easily sound more dynamic

It’s possible to make quite significant changes to the ultimate sound of the DX1 II, of course — those digital filters have a slight effect, but go crazy with the PEQ and you can achieve some pretty obvious alternations. What you can’t do, though, is defeat the things the Topping does well or fully correct its shortcomings.

With a 24bit/48kHz FLAC file of The Record by Boygenius playing in the Tidal desktop app and incoming via USB-C, it doesn’t take long at all to appreciate the facility the DX1 II has with detail retrieval. It’s alert to even the most minor, most subtle occurrences in the recording, keeps an eye on the low-level dynamics of harmonic over- and undertones, and deals with transients confidently too. It gives these details good weighting, so the emphasis is always on the music and not solely on how deeply into it the Topping can peer.

The tonal balance it strikes is naturalistic and pleasant, and its over-all character is, in the most positive way, easy-going and quite laid-back. It can do ‘urgency’ if it absolutely has to, of course, but its fundamental attitude is one that’s not in any way fatiguing. At no point is the Topping likely to grab you by the lapels — it’s altogether too grown-up and, again in a positive way, polite for that sort of behavior.

Some of this comes about because of its relative lack of dynamic impetus. The headline dynamics of ‘quiet’ and ‘LOUD!’ in a 16bit/44.1kHz file of Life Metal by Sunn O))) are somewhat flattened by the slight shortage of headroom the DX1 II exhibits. The distance between these two positions is not as pronounced as it is when described by a DAC/headphone amp that breathes a little more deeply. Some of it is due to the Topping’s slight-but-definite tendency to roll off the highest frequencies. There’s acceptable extension into the top end, but not quite the attack or even assertiveness that makes treble sounds properly bite and shine.

Elsewhere, though, the DX1 II is on firmer ground. It has a good understanding of rhythm and tempo, and controls its low-frequency activity to the point that there’s a proper sensation of fluency to the way rhythms are expressed. It can open up a soundstage to the point that even quite complex recordings get a little elbow-room, and the stage is also controlled well. And it’s worth noting that, unlike a couple of nominal rivals, the DX1 II doesn’t alter its behavior depending on the volume you’re listening at — even when playing very quietly or really quite loud, its sonic stance remains consistent.
- Sound quality score: 4 / 5
Topping DX1 II review: Design
- Aluminum chassis
- 32 x 100 x 100mm (HxWxD)

The DX1 II is usefully compact (just 32 x 100 x 100mm, HxWxD), so won’t hog space on your desktop or equipment rack. Built mostly from machined aluminum, it’s very well-made and finished — its edges are nicely rounded and it’s not remotely sharp at any of its corners.

At 275g, it’s unlikely to be towed around your desktop by heavy-cabled headphones, either. Only the fact that some of the socketry is quite close together on the rear panel (which is inevitable, really) precludes the use of chunkier, more premium cables and constitutes any kind of issue.
- Design score: 4.5 / 5
Topping DX1 II review: Usability & setup
- LED display
- Remote control handset
- Overworked fascia control dial

The majority of the fascia is occupied by a relatively large and gratifyingly legible LED display — volume level, selected input and what-have-you is all revealed. There’s also a relatively large turn/press dial that covers a lot of the device's functions. In all honesty, the dial is not especially intuitive when you want to do anything beyond change input or adjust volume — so it’s just as well Topping provides a little remote control handset that makes getting at your EQs, and all the rest of it, quite a lot more straightforward.

Set-up is the work of a moment, of course. You’ll need to connect the USB-C slot to a source of power — maybe this is also your source of music, if it isn’t then your source will need to be connected to the optical input. Then you need to connect the DX1 II to its output device — headphones, probably, or maybe the stereo RCA outputs to an amplifier or powered speaker. And then you’re in business.
- Usability & setup score: 4 / 5
Topping DX1 II review: Value
- Small but feels premium
- Good standard of build
- Out-and-out sound quality not up there (but you won't feel short-changed)

It may only be tiny, but Topping has managed to make the DX1 II feel and, to a lesser extent, look like it deserves to cost three figures. The standard of build is well up to snuff, too — and when you take the thoroughgoing nature of its specification into account, too, the sensation of value for money is hard to argue with.
The value proposition isn’t quite so cut-and-dried when it comes to out-and-out sound quality - but even here the DX1 II does more than enough right to prevent you feeling short-changed.
- Value score: 4.5 / 5
Should I buy the Topping DX1 II?
Buy it if…
You have a desktop audio system that just consists of a laptop and some headphones
Putting the DX1 II between the two will result in a significant uptick in audio quality.
You want to enhance your gaming experience
With UAC 1.0 selected, the signal from a console incoming and some appropriate headphones attached, gaming becomes a much more immersive experience.
You have some power-hungry headphones
The Topping’s balanced output is rated at 2 x 1000mW into 32 ohms, which is more than enough to deal even quite tricky headphones.
Don't buy it if…
You’re easily frustrated
The fascia controls are not what you’d call ‘intuitive’.
You enjoy the dynamic aspects of music reproduction
The DX1 II is unwilling or unable to put really convincing distance between dynamic extremes .
You’re especially attuned to high-frequency sound
You can fiddle with the PEQ and/or the filters all you like — the Topping is inclined to roll off the top end at least a little.
Topping DX1 II review: Also consider

It’s more affordable than the DX1 II — and it looks and feels it, too — but the iFi Uno is a high-achieving little device that offers a direct, confident and information-rich sound no matter the source of music it’s connected to.
How I tested the Topping DX1 II
I used the Topping DX1 II with an Apple MacBook Pro — connecting to the USB-C slot allowed for data transfer and power supply at the same time, and gave access to numerous music streaming services.

I connected a pair of Sennheiser IE900 wired in-ear headphones to the unbalanced 3.5mm output, and also to the balanced 4.4mm output (the Sennheiser have a selection of cables with different terminations).
I also connected a Sony PlayStation 5 via the optical input and sent the DX1 II output signal to the preamp in my reference system via its RCA outputs.

articles.headline: Carrick future in huge doubt as Man Utd consider alternatives
keyFacts: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick faces an uncertain future after a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth extended their winless run to eight matches.
Sky Sports News understands club executives were already considering alternatives, and insiders expect Carrick to be dismissed following the poor results.
Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe have been identified as the frontrunners to replace Carrick should he leave the club.
body: Michael Carrick Man Utd future: Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann expected frontrunners if head coach departs
Man Utd beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford to heap the pressure on head coach Michael Carrick; Captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped and United are eight games without a win
Sunday 25 October 2026 18:45, UK
Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach is hanging by a thread.

United plunged to a new low on Sunday as they were beaten 3-0 at Old Trafford by Bournemouth. The defeat extends their winless run to eight matches and leaves United just above the Premier League relegation zone.

Sky Sports News understands that United's bosses were already considering alternatives for the head coach role even before the defeat to Bournemouth amid the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season.
